lawyer:
T. Ali, Sr. Advocate, with Md. Yahya, Advocate, instructed by A. Rab-II, Advocate on-Record ------ For the Appellants.
Sultan Hossain Khan, Dy. Attorney-General, with B.B. Roy Chowdhury, Asstt. Attorney-General, instructed by S.S. Hoda, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent No. 1. Respondent No. 2-Dead. Respondent No. 3 and 4-Ex-parte.
parties:
Abu Saber Aziz Mohammad and others ------ Appellants.
Vs.
Government & others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 2. The appellants' case in the that the disputed lands were thrown up in the bed of the river Jhurjhuria as char lands lying to the contiguous north of the two mouzas known as Kanchi Harania and Shankar Kati within P.S. Shamnagar District Khulna that in 1953 when the said char became fit for cultivation, the Government of East Pakistan started Settlement Case No. 9/53-54 for settle went of the said char lands, that Appellant No. 1 having applied for settlement of the land on behalf of all the appellants, the Khas Mahal Officer proposed to settle the disputed land permanently with them by his order dated 8-7-53, which was duly approved by the Collector of Khulna and subsequently also by the Board of Revenue, that Appellant No. 1 paid the Salami money and rent to the Government and executed a Kabuliyat on 15.9.53 in favour of the Collector of Khulna, who accepted the same, that the area of the land under settlement measured 18.34 acres, which subsequently increased to 27.63 acres by accretion, that this entire 27.63 acres of land were wrongly recorded in the Khas Khatian of Respondents No. 2 to 4 that after the acquisition of the rent receiving interests and the excess Khas lands of the said Respondents they said lands had been suit was recorded in the Khas Khatian of the Government, Respondent No. 1, that the Government Tahshilder settled some of the lands described in Schedule B to the plaint with the local cultivators, who had cut away the paddy grown by the appellants in the said lands and that the Government, Respondent No. 1, had been threatening to dispossess the appellants from the lands of Schedule A also.
